directAnswer: St. Felix III was a Roman of noble family who served as pope from 483 to 492. He excommunicated Patriarch Acacius of Constantinople in 484 for supporting Emperor Zeno's Henotikon, beginning the Acacian schism between Rome and the East that lasted until 519. He was an ancestor of Pope St. Gregory the Great.

paras: Felix became pope in March 483, shortly after Emperor Zeno issued the Henotikon, a doctrinal compromise that sidestepped the Council of Chalcedon. Patriarch Acacius of Constantinople supported it and entered communion with Peter Mongus of Alexandria, whom Rome considered a heretic.

Felix sent two bishops, Vitalis and Misenus, to Constantinople to demand that Acacius explain himself. Under pressure there, they communicated with Acacius's party. On their return, a Roman synod deposed them, and in 484 Felix excommunicated Acacius. The break, known as the Acacian schism, outlasted both men and was healed only under Pope Hormisdas in 519.

sections.h2: Family, Africa, and a Confusing Number
paras: Felix was a widower with children when he became pope. Gregory the Great, writing a century later, refers to him as his ancestor, usually understood as his great-great-grandfather. The Liber Pontificalis says he came from a Roman senatorial family.

He also dealt with the aftermath of the Vandal persecution in North Africa, where some Catholics had been forcibly rebaptized by Arians; a Roman synod set terms of penance for their reconciliation. Felix is sometimes called Felix II because the earlier Felix, installed during the exile of Liberius, is now regarded as an antipope. He died on March 1, 492, and was buried at St. Paul Outside the Walls.

keyFacts: Pope from 483 to 492; from a Roman noble family
Excommunicated Patriarch Acacius in 484, beginning the Acacian schism
Set penances for Africans forcibly rebaptized during the Vandal persecution
Ancestor of Pope St. Gregory the Great
Sometimes numbered Felix II; feast day March 1

faqs.question: What was the Acacian schism?
faqs.answer: It was a break in communion between Rome and Constantinople that began when Felix III excommunicated Patriarch Acacius in 484 for backing the Henotikon. It ended in 519 under Pope Hormisdas.

faqs.question: Why is Pope Felix III sometimes called Felix II?
faqs.answer: The Felix installed during Pope Liberius's exile is now counted as an antipope. Lists that omit him number this pope as Felix II, but the official numbering keeps Felix III.

faqs.question: Was Pope Felix III related to Gregory the Great?
faqs.answer: Yes. Gregory the Great describes him as an ancestor, usually identified as his great-great-grandfather. Felix had been married with children before becoming pope.
